definition: Chest pain/pressure/heaviness/tightness that may be cardiac (not pain clearly caused by an injury, cough or meals), OR new cardiac-equivalent symptoms today in a diabetic/elderly patient (sudden uneasiness 'ghabrahat' with sweating, breathlessness or epigastric 'gas' discomfort)
Sudden face droop, one-sided arm/leg weakness, or slurred/absent speech (FAST)
Severe breathing difficulty: cannot speak full sentences, struggling to breathe, chest indrawing in a sick child, choking on a foreign body
New confusion, drowsiness (including sleepiness after a fit), not recognising family, unresponsive
Fits/convulsions now or within the last few hours
Vomiting blood, black tarry stools, coughing up large amounts of blood (a wound bleeding that will not stop is uncontrolled major bleeding = Level 1)
Vaginal bleeding in pregnancy, or heavy bleeding after delivery
Pregnant (>20 weeks) or recently delivered with severe headache, blurred vision, upper-abdominal pain, face/hand swelling, or fits
Third-trimester pregnancy with reduced or absent baby movements
Swallowed pesticide/insecticide, rat poison, kerosene or an overdose of tablets, or pesticide exposure while spraying with symptoms
Any snakebite (even without symptoms yet)
Scorpion sting with sweating, vomiting, cold limbs or breathlessness, or any sting in a child
Diarrhoea/vomiting with signs of severe dehydration: lethargic, sunken eyes, unable to drink, very slow skin pinch, fainting, very little urine
Infant younger than 3 months with temperature >= 38.0 C
Child under 5 years who is unable to drink/breastfeed, vomiting everything, lethargic/unconscious, or has had convulsions (WHO IMCI general danger signs)
Fever with cold limbs/cold clammy skin or very little urine (any age); fever with confusion in a patient aged 15+ (without neck stiffness); or ANY fever in a patient on cancer chemotherapy

Fever with neck stiffness (any age), or fever with confusion/unresponsiveness in a child under 15 (meningitis/encephalitis/AES). A fit with fever in a child 6 months-5 years who is only sleepy afterwards is a febrile seizure (RF_SEIZURE), not this flag

Suspected dengue: an acute fever (2-7 days) with NO other obvious source (no loose motions, no burning urine, no vaginal discharge, no pain localised to the right lower or lower/pelvic abdomen, no jaundice) PLUS a warning sign: abdominal pain, persistent vomiting (vomiting everything), bleeding gums/nose, black stools, lethargy/restlessness, or giddiness (cold clammy skin with collapse = shock = Level 1)
Thoughts of self-harm or suicide, or a self-harm attempt (including a poisoning where the complaint mentions intent, e.g. after a quarrel / 'does not want to live')
Acutely agitated/violent behaviour, danger to others

High-risk injury: high-energy road accident (hit by truck/bus, thrown off a vehicle, injuries at many places, cannot get up) or any road accident with a head injury or bleeding that will not stop; fall from height (roof, tree, first floor); head injury with blackout/vomiting/confusion. A simple slip or fall with one swollen/bent limb is a suspected fracture (Level 3), not this flag
Allergic reaction with lip/tongue/face swelling or breathing difficulty (throat closing or collapse = Level 1)
Diabetic with very high sugar plus vomiting, abdominal pain, deep fast breathing or drowsiness
Diabetic on insulin/sugar tablets with sweating, shaking, odd behaviour or confusion
Very hot body after heat exposure with confusion or collapse (heat stroke, not counted as sepsis/meningitis; Level 2 for new confusion unless a Level-1 sign or vital is present)
Severe abdominal pain with hard/distended belly, no stool or gas, stuck painful hernia, or (in a woman with a missed period) severe one-sided pain
Sudden, severe 'worst-ever' headache
Sudden severe testicular pain
Chemical/lime splash into the eye or sudden loss of vision
Large burns, burns of face/chest, or burns with breathing problems
